title: Configure and verify inside source NAT using static and pools

questions.question: What does NAT primarily do?
choices: Maps private IPs to public IPs
questions.explanation: NAT maps inside local (private) to inside global (public) addresses.

correct.explanation: NAT translates private ↔ public addresses so internal hosts reach the Internet with routable addresses.

incorrect.explanation: Encryption is IPsec/VPN — NAT only changes addresses/port mappings.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: NAT encrypts traffic
incorrect.whatItDoes: Encrypts traffic points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for nat purpose.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "nat purpose", Maps private IPs to public IPs satisfies what this question tests — Encrypts traffic does not.

incorrect.explanation: Inter-VLAN routing uses a router/L3 switch — NAT is address translation at the edge.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: NAT routes VLANs
incorrect.whatItDoes: Routes between VLANs points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for nat purpose.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "nat purpose", Maps private IPs to public IPs satisfies what this question tests — Routes between VLANs does not.

incorrect.explanation: DHCP assigns addresses — NAT rewrites them on the way out.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: NAT vs DHCP
incorrect.whatItDoes: Assigns DHCP addresses points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for nat purpose.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "nat purpose", Maps private IPs to public IPs satisfies what this question tests — Assigns DHCP addresses does not.

answerReview.examTip: Private inside → NAT → public outside. PAT overloads one public IP.

questions.question: Many home devices share a single public IP. Which NAT type is this?
questions.explanation: PAT/overload maps many inside hosts to one public IP using ports.

correct.explanation: PAT (NAT overload) maps many inside private hosts to one public IP using unique source ports.

incorrect.explanation: Static NAT is 1:1 permanent mapping — many home devices sharing one public IP needs port-based overload.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using 1:1 static NAT for many-to-one scenario
incorrect.whatItDoes: Static NAT points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for PAT/overload maps many inside hosts to one public IP using ports.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "PAT/overload maps many inside hosts to one public IP using ports", PAT (overload) satisfies what this question tests — Static NAT does not.

incorrect.explanation: Dynamic NAT pools one public IP per session but still exhausts the pool with many simultaneous hosts — PAT scales with ports.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Choosing dynamic pool when overload/PAT is required
incorrect.whatItDoes: Dynamic NAT points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for PAT/overload maps many inside hosts to one public IP using ports.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "PAT/overload maps many inside hosts to one public IP using ports", PAT (overload) satisfies what this question tests — Dynamic NAT does not.

incorrect.explanation: Without NAT, private RFC1918 addresses cannot reach the public Internet from a typical home ISP setup.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Denying NAT in a classic SOHO sharing scenario
incorrect.whatItDoes: No NAT points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for PAT/overload maps many inside hosts to one public IP using ports.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "PAT/overload maps many inside hosts to one public IP using ports", PAT (overload) satisfies what this question tests — No NAT does not.

answerReview.examTip: Many inside → one public IP = PAT/overload, not static 1:1.

questions.question: Which command creates a permanent 1:1 mapping for a server?
choices: ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload
questions.explanation: Static NAT uses ip nat inside source static <local> <global>.

correct.explanation: ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.10 203.0.113.10 creates a permanent inside-local to inside-global 1:1 mapping.

incorrect.explanation: ip nat pool defines addresses for dynamic NAT — static 1:1 server publishing uses inside source static.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using dynamic pool command for static server mapping
incorrect.whatItDoes: ip nat pool points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for static nat.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "static nat", ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.10 203.0.113.10 satisfies what this question tests — ip nat pool does not.

incorrect.explanation: That overload line enables PAT for an ACL — static server publishing needs explicit local/global pair.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Applying PAT overload syntax to 1:1 static requirement
incorrect.whatItDoes: ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload implies many-inside-to-few-outside PAT/overload translation.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: NAT type (static nat): ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.10 203.0.113.10 fits the stem — ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload describes PAT/overload when the question tests a different translation style.

incorrect.explanation: ip nat outside only labels interface direction — it does not create the static translation entry.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Stopping at interface NAT label without translation rule
incorrect.whatItDoes: ip nat outside points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for static nat.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "static nat", ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.10 203.0.113.10 satisfies what this question tests — ip nat outside does not.

answerReview.examTip: Permanent server NAT → ip nat inside source static <local> <global>.

questions.question: NAT is configured but nothing is translated. What is most often missing?
choices: The ip nat inside / ip nat outside interface tags
questions.explanation: Interfaces must be marked ip nat inside and ip nat outside.

correct.explanation: NAT requires ip nat inside and ip nat outside on the correct interfaces — without these tags, translation never occurs.

incorrect.explanation: A default route helps reach the Internet but does not enable NAT — inside/outside interface designation is mandatory.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Adding default route when NAT direction tags are missing
incorrect.whatItDoes: A default route points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for interface tags.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "interface tags", The ip nat inside / ip nat outside interface tags satisfies what this question tests — A default route does not.

incorrect.explanation: Loopbacks are not required for basic NAT — the missing inside/outside labels prevent any translation.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Creating loopback instead of labeling NAT interfaces
incorrect.whatItDoes: A loopback points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for interface tags.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "interface tags", The ip nat inside / ip nat outside interface tags satisfies what this question tests — A loopback does not.

incorrect.explanation: DNS resolves names — NAT operates on IP headers and needs inside/outside interface roles defined first.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Checking DNS when NAT interface roles are unset
incorrect.whatItDoes: DNS points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for interface tags.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "interface tags", The ip nat inside / ip nat outside interface tags satisfies what this question tests — DNS does not.

answerReview.examTip: NAT broken? First check ip nat inside / ip nat outside on the right interfaces.

questions.question: Which command configures PAT to the outside interface?
choices: ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload
questions.explanation: PAT: ip nat inside source list <ACL> interface <if> overload.

correct.explanation: ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload enables PAT using the outside interface address.

incorrect.explanation: Static NAT maps one inside to one outside — PAT needs overload on an interface or pool.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using static syntax for many-to-one PAT
incorrect.whatItDoes: ip nat inside source static points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for overload command.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "overload command", ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload satisfies what this question tests — ip nat inside source static does not.

incorrect.explanation: A NAT pool supports dynamic NAT — PAT overload typically uses the outside interface keyword with overload.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting pool alone to provide PAT
incorrect.whatItDoes: ip nat pool MYPOOL points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for overload command.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "overload command", ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload satisfies what this question tests — ip nat pool MYPOOL does not.

incorrect.explanation: Outside source NAT reverses direction — inside hosts sharing one public IP use inside source with overload.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Configuring outside source for inside PAT
incorrect.whatItDoes: ip nat outside source list 1 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for overload command.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "overload command", ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload satisfies what this question tests — ip nat outside source list 1 does not.

answerReview.examTip: PAT to outside interface → ip nat inside source list <acl> interface <if> overload.

questions.question: A host’s private address as seen inside the network is called its…
questions.explanation: Inside local = the private address of an inside host.

correct.explanation: Inside local is the host private address as known on the internal network before translation.

incorrect.explanation: Inside global is the translated public address as seen externally — not the private address inside the LAN.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Swapping inside local with inside global
incorrect.whatItDoes: Inside global assigns a specific NAT address role (inside/outside, local/global) that may not match the stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "terminology", Inside local satisfies what this question tests — Inside global does not.

incorrect.explanation: Outside global is the remote public address — inside local refers to the internal host private IP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Labeling remote public as inside local
incorrect.whatItDoes: Outside global assigns a specific NAT address role (inside/outside, local/global) that may not match the stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "terminology", Inside local satisfies what this question tests — Outside global does not.

incorrect.explanation: Outside local is how the internal network sees an outside address — not the host private IP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing outside local with host private address
incorrect.whatItDoes: Outside local assigns a specific NAT address role (inside/outside, local/global) that may not match the stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "terminology", Inside local satisfies what this question tests — Outside local does not.

answerReview.examTip: NAT naming: inside local = private IP before translation on the LAN.

questions.question: Which command shows active NAT translations?
questions.explanation: show ip nat translations lists the current mappings.

correct.explanation: show ip nat translations displays active inside/outside address mappings currently in the NAT table.

incorrect.explanation: show ip route lists routing table entries — NAT translations live in the NAT table, not the RIB.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using routing table for NAT translation verification
incorrect.whatItDoes: show ip route is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (show ip nat translations lists the current mappings): show ip nat translations inspects the right table or state — show ip route shows unrelated information.

incorrect.explanation: Running-config shows configured NAT policies — active live translations require show ip nat translations.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Checking running-config for active translation state
incorrect.whatItDoes: show running-config is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (show ip nat translations lists the current mappings): show ip nat translations inspects the right table or state — show running-config shows unrelated information.

incorrect.explanation: show ip nat inside is not standard verification syntax — use show ip nat translations for the translation table.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Inventing show ip nat inside command
incorrect.whatItDoes: show ip nat inside is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (show ip nat translations lists the current mappings): show ip nat translations inspects the right table or state — show ip nat inside shows unrelated information.

answerReview.examTip: Active NAT entries → show ip nat translations.

questions.question: True or False: PAT distinguishes multiple inside hosts behind one public IP using port numbers.
questions.explanation: True — PAT tracks translations by inside global IP + port.

correct.explanation: PAT (overload) multiplexes many inside hosts on one public IP using unique source port numbers.

incorrect.explanation: Without port translation, multiple hosts cannot share one public IP simultaneously — that is PAT's role.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Denying port role in PAT
incorrect.whatItDoes: False states the opposite of the tested fact about pat ports.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "pat ports", True satisfies what this question tests — False does not.

answerReview.examTip: PAT = one public IP + many hosts distinguished by ports.

questions.question: Which method will allow you to use RFC 1918 addresses for Internet requests?

correct.explanation: NAT translates private RFC 1918 addresses to public addresses so internal hosts can reach the Internet.

incorrect.explanation: CIDR is efficient address allocation notation — it does not translate private addresses for Internet access.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Equating CIDR with address translation
incorrect.whatItDoes: CIDR points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for addresses.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "addresses", NAT satisfies what this question tests — CIDR does not.

incorrect.explanation: Classful addressing is obsolete — RFC 1918 private space still needs NAT (or proxy) to reach public Internet.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting classful rules to enable Internet from private space
incorrect.whatItDoes: Classful addressing points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for addresses.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "addresses", NAT satisfies what this question tests — Classful addressing does not.

incorrect.explanation: VPN encrypts/tunnels traffic — the question asks how RFC 1918 hosts reach the Internet, which is NAT/PAT.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Choosing VPN when NAT is the standard exam answer
incorrect.whatItDoes: VPN points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for addresses.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "addresses", NAT satisfies what this question tests — VPN does not.

answerReview.examTip: Private RFC 1918 → Internet = NAT/PAT. Label inside/outside first.

questions.question:
NAT topology:
- Host A (inside local): 192.168.1.2 on LAN
- Router A Gi0/0 (192.168.1.1): ip nat inside
- Router A S0/0 (inside global): 179.43.44.1 — ip nat outside
- Internet → Web server (outside global): 198.23.53.3
- Internal web server inside local: 192.168.1.3 (static NAT to 179.43.44.1)
- Enterprise public pool: 179.43.44.0/28 (usable 179.43.44.2–179.43.44.15)
- Inside network: 192.168.1.0/24

what is the inside local IP address?

correct.explanation: Inside local is the private address as the host sees it — typically the LAN host (192.168.1.2 Host A).

incorrect.explanation: 192.168.1.1 is the inside router interface, not the host's inside local address.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing router inside interface with host
incorrect.whatItDoes: 192.168.1.1 Router A Gi0/0 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (inside local): 192.168.1.2 Host A matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — 192.168.1.1 Router A Gi0/0 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: 179.43.44.1 is a public/outside-side address on the WAN, not inside local.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Labeling WAN address as inside local
incorrect.whatItDoes: 179.43.44.1 Router A S0/0 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (inside local): 192.168.1.2 Host A matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — 179.43.44.1 Router A S0/0 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: 198.23.53.3 is an outside global server, not the inside local host.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Mixing outside global with inside local
incorrect.whatItDoes: 198.23.53.3 web server points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for inside local.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "inside local", 192.168.1.2 Host A satisfies what this question tests — 198.23.53.3 web server does not.

answerReview.examTip: Inside local = private host address before NAT.

questions.question: When configuring dynamic NAT, why must you configure an access list?
choices: The access list allows incoming access from outside global addresses.
The access list allows outgoing access from inside local addresses.
The access list allows outgoing access from outside local addresses.
The access list allows outgoing access from inside global addresses.

correct.explanation: The access list defines which inside local addresses are permitted to be translated by the NAT pool or PAT configuration.

incorrect.explanation: Dynamic NAT ACLs identify inside local sources eligible for translation — they do not permit inbound access from outside global addresses.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Reversing inside/outside direction for NAT ACL
incorrect.whatItDoes: The access list allows incoming access from outside global addresses. assigns a specific NAT address role (inside/outside, local/global) that may not match the stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: NAT address roles (configuring dynamic NAT, why must you configure an access list) are fixed — The access list allows outgoing access from inside local addresses. matches the stem's inside/outside and local/global pairing; The access list allows incoming access from outside global addresses. swaps roles.

incorrect.explanation: Outside local addresses are on the outside segment as seen locally — the NAT ACL matches inside local sources going out, not outside local.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing outside local with inside local in NAT ACL
incorrect.whatItDoes: The access list allows outgoing access from outside local addresses. assigns a specific NAT address role (inside/outside, local/global) that may not match the stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: NAT address roles (configuring dynamic NAT, why must you configure an access list) are fixed — The access list allows outgoing access from inside local addresses. matches the stem's inside/outside and local/global pairing; The access list allows outgoing access from outside local addresses. swaps roles.

incorrect.explanation: Inside global is the translated address — the ACL specifies which inside local hosts may use NAT, not inside global as the matched source.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Matching inside global instead of inside local in ACL
incorrect.whatItDoes: The access list allows outgoing access from inside global addresses. assigns a specific NAT address role (inside/outside, local/global) that may not match the stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: NAT address roles (configuring dynamic NAT, why must you configure an access list) are fixed — The access list allows outgoing access from inside local addresses. matches the stem's inside/outside and local/global pairing; The access list allows outgoing access from inside global addresses. swaps roles.

answerReview.examTip: NAT ACL must match inside local addresses permitted to translate.

questions.question: Which command wipe out all current NAT translations in the NAT table?

correct.explanation: clear ip nat translation * removes all dynamic (and static if specified) entries from the translation table.

incorrect.explanation: no ip nat translation is not the clear command syntax.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using no instead of clear
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#no ip nat translation points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for translations.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "translations", Router#clear ip nat translation * satisfies what this question tests — Router#no ip nat translation does not.

incorrect.explanation: Clear requires translation and usually * for all entries.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Incomplete clear syntax
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#clear ip nat translation points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for translations.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "translations", Router#clear ip nat translation * satisfies what this question tests — Router#clear ip nat translation does not.

incorrect.explanation: clear ip nat without translation/* is incomplete.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Truncated clear command
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#clear ip nat points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for translations.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "translations", Router#clear ip nat translation * satisfies what this question tests — Router#clear ip nat does not.

answerReview.examTip: Flush NAT table → clear ip nat translation *.

questions.question: Which command can see real-time network address translations?

correct.explanation: debug ip nat shows real-time NAT translation events (use sparingly in production).

incorrect.explanation: show ip translations is invalid — use show ip nat translations or debug.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Invalid show command
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ip translations is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "translations", Router#debug ip nat satisfies what this question tests — Router#show ip translations does not.

incorrect.explanation: debug ip translations is not standard IOS NAT debug syntax.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Wrong debug keyword
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#debug ip translations points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for translations.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "translations", Router#debug ip nat satisfies what this question tests — Router#debug ip translations does not.

incorrect.explanation: show ip nat alone is incomplete for realtime events — debug is required.

answerReview.examTip: Realtime NAT events → debug ip nat (remember undebug all).

which command will configure Port Address Translation?

incorrect.explanation: No overload keyword means dynamic NAT, not PAT on a single public IP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Pool without overload on one IP
incorrect.whatItDoes: RouterA(config)#access-list 1 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 RouterA(config)#ip nat pool EntPool 179.43.44.1 179.43.44.1 netmask 255.255.255.0 RouterA(config)#ip nat inside source list 1 pool EntPool applies an ACL type (standard vs extended) or number range that may not match placement rules here.

questions.question: Which method will allow you to use RFC 1918 addresses for Internet requests?

correct.explanation: NAT translates private RFC 1918 addresses to routable public addresses so inside hosts can reach the Internet.

incorrect.explanation: CIDR is an addressing/aggregation scheme — it does not translate private addresses for Internet egress.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting CIDR to provide private-to-public translation
incorrect.whatItDoes: CIDR points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for addresses.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "addresses", NAT satisfies what this question tests — CIDR does not.

incorrect.explanation: Classful addressing is a legacy model — RFC 1918 hosts still need NAT (or similar) to reach the public Internet.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Believing classful rules alone enable Internet use of RFC 1918
incorrect.whatItDoes: Classful addressing points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for addresses.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "addresses", NAT satisfies what this question tests — Classful addressing does not.

incorrect.explanation: VPNs tunnel traffic between sites — they do not by themselves translate RFC 1918 hosts to public Internet addresses.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Substituting VPN for address translation to the Internet
incorrect.whatItDoes: VPN points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for addresses.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "addresses", NAT satisfies what this question tests — VPN does not.

answerReview.examTip: RFC 1918 → Internet egress needs NAT (or carrier-grade NAT) to a public address.
